newsitem.title: USA: SBC chief could lead combined firm - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SBC chief could lead combined firm - WSJ.

text.p: A merger between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Corp, if it's pulled off, could lead to SBC Chairman Edward Whitacre being named chief executive and eventually chairman of the new entity, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said such a scenario would leave AT&T Chairman Robert Allen's handpicked successor, President John Walter, unable to fulfill the plan of his being appointed to those top posts.
"You can only end up with one chief," an unnamed industry executive who knows the three men told the Journal. "I can't imagine Whitacre agreeing to a deal unless he is CEO."

The Journal on Tuesday had reported that the two telecommunications companies are in the midst of merger talks in a deal valued at more than $50 billion, leading to wide speculation about management changes that would ensue.

The CNBC financial cable TV channel reported on Tuesday that a plan was under discussion in which Walter, who joined AT&T seven months ago, would become chief executive of the combined companies and Whitacre would become a non-executive chairman, with a strategic planning role.
